q: Determine which climate is generally humid, stays above about 18°C, and may have year-round rainfall or distinct wet and dry seasons.
n: Tropical climates are characterized by consistently warm conditions; many tropical regions are humid and receive substantial rainfall, with patterns varying by monsoon influence. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Tropical climate.

q: Identify what term describes air moving through a building from a windward opening toward a leeward opening.
n: Cross ventilation uses pressure differences between openings on different sides of a building to move outdoor air through occupied spaces. Source: Whole Building Design Guide — Natural Ventilation.

q: Work out which color is commonly described as bright and attention-getting, but can contribute to visual fatigue when overused.
n: Yellow is highly luminous and visually attention-getting; intense yellow can become tiring when used extensively. Source: Interaction Design Foundation — Color Psychology.

q: Figure out which designer is most strongly associated with the French formal garden tradition and the Gardens of Versailles.
n: André Le Nôtre was the principal designer of the Gardens of Versailles and is strongly associated with the formal jardin à la française tradition. Source: Château de Versailles — André Le Nôtre.

q: State which architect designed Park Güell, the Barcelona landmark later included in UNESCO's World Heritage listing of his works.
n: Park Güell is one of the properties included in UNESCO's World Heritage listing of Antoni Gaudí's works, inscribed in 1984. Source: UNESCO World Heritage Centre — Works of Antoni Gaudí.

q: Indicate which building side is generally the better choice for extensive full-height glazing in a northern-hemisphere passive-design context.
n: North-facing glazing receives relatively diffuse light and less direct solar heat than east- or west-facing glazing; this is a common passive-design strategy in northern-hemisphere contexts. Source: Whole Building Design Guide — Daylighting.

q: Name the property describes how light or dark—a color's perceived brilliance or intensity—appears that In color theory,.
n: Value describes the lightness or darkness of a color, distinguishing lighter and darker versions of a hue. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Color.

q: Determine who is recognized as the Father of Philippine Landscape Architecture and was named a National Artist for Architecture.
n: Ildefonso P. Santos Jr. pioneered landscape architecture practice in the Philippines and was recognized as the Father of Philippine Landscape Architecture; he was conferred National Artist for Architecture in 2006. Source: National Commission for Culture and the Arts.

q: Identify which term best describes a planned outdoor area that is often large and intended for public use.
n: A park is a planned outdoor area maintained for recreation, amenity, or public enjoyment; an urban park is a specific type of park within a city. Source: National Park Service — What Is a Park?

q: Work out what design approach reduces dependence on mechanical systems by using building form, orientation, and construction to maintain comfort.
n: Passive design uses site, orientation, envelope, shading, ventilation, and related architectural strategies to achieve comfort with reduced mechanical energy use. Source: U.S. Department of Energy — Passive Solar Home Design.

q: Figure out which lighting type is intended to illuminate a specific task or work area.
n: Task lighting is directed to a particular surface or area so that visual tasks can be performed effectively. Source: Illuminating Engineering Society — Task Lighting.

q: State what is the commonly used depth for a kitchen counter.
n: A 600 mm depth is a common standard for kitchen worktops and base-cabinet runs. Source: Bimstore — Kitchen Counter specification example.

q: Indicate which choice is an example of softscape.
n: Bushes are living plant material, so they belong to the softscape category; decks, trellises, and arbors are constructed elements. Source: U.S. EPA — Green Infrastructure.

q: Establish what term refers to the amount of water vapor present in the atmosphere.
n: Humidity is the amount of water vapor in the air. Source: National Weather Service — Humidity.

q: Determine what Philippine architectural feature is a small opening below a larger window, often fitted with grilles or balusters, that admits air and light.
n: A ventanilla is a small opening below a larger window, commonly found in the bahay na bato, that can admit additional air and light and may be screened with balusters or grilles. Source: Ventanilla (Philippine architecture).

q: Identify which discipline studies interactions between people and systems to improve human well-being and overall performance.
n: Ergonomics (human factors) focuses on optimizing systems by considering human capabilities, limitations, and interactions. Source: International Ergonomics Association — Definition and Domains.

q: Work out what term refers to constructed elements and materials used in landscape design.
n: Hardscape refers to the built, non-living components of a landscape, such as paving, walls, and other constructed features. Source: Landscape Architecture Foundation — Landscape terminology.

q: Figure out what term means the typical atmospheric conditions of a place over a long period.
n: Climate describes the long-term pattern of weather conditions in a region, while weather refers to shorter-term atmospheric conditions. Source: NOAA — What Is Climate?

q: State which factor can strongly influence a building's natural cooling potential.
n: Wind drives air movement through and around a building, supporting natural ventilation and convective cooling. Source: Whole Building Design Guide — Natural Ventilation.

q: Indicate what do you call colors positioned next to one another on the color wheel.
n: Analogous colors are neighboring hues on the color wheel and are commonly used together for visually related color schemes. Source: Adobe Color terminology.

q: Establish who is widely regarded as the father of modern American landscape architecture and co-designed New York's Central Park.
n: Frederick Law Olmsted is widely recognized as a founder of American landscape architecture and is closely associated with the design of Central Park with Calvert Vaux. Source: U.S. National Park Service — Olmsted.

q: Determine what term describes a planned outdoor area intended for displaying, cultivating, or enjoying plants and nature.
n: A garden is a deliberately planned space in which plants are cultivated, displayed, or enjoyed. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Garden.

q: Determine the facade pair receives the greatest direct solar heat exposure over the day that In the source's tropical-building context,.
n: East and west facades receive low-angle morning and afternoon sun, which can create substantial solar heat gain that is harder to shade with horizontal overhangs. Source: Whole Building Design Guide — Orientation and Solar Control.

q: Work out which option is not itself an artificial light source.
n: A solar panel converts sunlight into electricity; it is not a lighting fixture by itself. Desk, street, and bollard lights are artificial lighting installations. Source: U.S. Department of Energy — Solar Photovoltaic Technology Basics.

q: Figure out what is the name of the traditional Chinese practice of arranging environments to promote harmony and balance.
n: Feng shui is a Chinese system of arranging space and orientation in relation to principles of harmony and balance. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica — Feng Shui.

q: Select the option that does NOT hardscape element?.
n: Ground covers are plants and therefore softscape. Bollards, riprap, and paved walks are constructed landscape elements. Source: U.S. EPA — Green Infrastructure.

q: Indicate which Philippine monsoon is locally called Amihan.
n: PAGASA identifies Amihan as the Northeast Monsoon, characterized by cold winds from the northeast and associated rainfall patterns. Source: DOST-PAGASA — Climate Advisories.

q: Establish what term describes the detailed process of analyzing space needs and choosing an efficient layout for a facility.
n: Space planning examines how a facility's spaces will be used and arranges them to meet functional needs efficiently. Source: Whole Building Design Guide — Space Planning.

q: Determine what is the typical commercial height range for a standard dining table.
n: A standard dining table is generally about 28–30 inches (roughly 71–76 cm) high. Source: Gavigan's — Dining Table Size & Clearance Guide.

q: Identify which landscape-design category consists primarily of living horticultural elements.
n: Softscape refers to living or plant-based components of a landscape, including trees, shrubs, groundcover, and other vegetation. Source: U.S. EPA — Green Landscaping.
